extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal financial assistance in health care (hospitals, providers, insurers), legal counsel, advocacy groups, and stakeholders commenting on or subject to HHS OCR's Section 1557 rule
extracted.subtask_description: Administrative rules and criteria governing how recipients may notify OCR that Federal religious freedom or conscience laws exempt them from particular provisions of the Section 1557 rule, and how OCR will process, temporarily exempt, determine, and allow appeal of such requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private right of action under section 1557
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts have long recognized that section 1557 authorizes a private right of action under any of the bases for discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR declines to revise regulatory text to adopt a stance on the appropriate standards that apply to private litigants; standards for private suits are to be addressed by Federal courts, not via agency rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age Act administrative-exhaustion concern
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters requested clarity that the Age Act's administrative exhaustion requirement (42 U.S.C. 6104(f)) should not prevent filing a court action involving multiple bases of discrimination that includes age.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR declined to revise regulatory text on this issue, noting that it is appropriately addressed by the Federal judicial branch rather than via agency rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to file OCR complaints (providers and relatives)
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals—including providers and relatives of a plan holder—who believe they have experienced discrimination prohibited by section 1557 are able to file a complaint with OCR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR cannot provide legal advice on whether a civil claim under section 1557 is appropriate; OCR will conduct a case-by-case analysis to determine its jurisdiction over complaint allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCR is primary enforcement agency within Department
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR is the agency within the Department that investigates and enforces section 1557 complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR continues to work with other agencies on initiatives and issues, but it will not revise the rule to empower other Department components to investigate/enforce section 1557 claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement posture and use of enforcement discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR will not postpone enforcement past the effective date (60 days after publication of the final rule) and declines broad postponement requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR has provided delayed implementation dates for some provisions; prior to taking an enforcement action (e.g., terminating Federal financial assistance or referring to DOJ), OCR must attempt to achieve a covered entity's voluntary compliance (such as providing technical assistance and reviewing policies and procedures). OCR may use enforcement discretion in particular circumstances but will not broadly delay enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and public posting of complaint/resolution information
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters recommended OCR publish general information about complaints received/resolved and post resolution agreements quickly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR already provides much of the requested information to Congress annually through Congressional Justifications and posts resolution agreements to its website; OCR intends to continue posting resolution agreements as cases are resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCR scope regarding private arbitration agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters asked OCR to prohibit insurers from requiring binding arbitration as the exclusive means to resolve a Section 1557 complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR considers agreements between private parties to be beyond the scope of this rulemaking and did not include such a prohibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: §92.302(a) — Reliance on Federal religious freedom and conscience protections
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may rely on applicable Federal protections for religious freedom and conscience; application of a particular provision(s) of this part to specific contexts, procedures, or health care services shall not be required where such protections apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This language is consistent with §92.3(c) and will be interpreted and applied in light of RFRA and other relevant statutes; OCR will faithfully apply legal standards set forth in the religious freedom or conscience law at issue and consult appropriate Department staff when enforcing the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: §92.302(b) — Notification/assurance request content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient's notification seeking assurance of an exemption must be in writing directed to the OCR Director and include: (1) identification of the particular provision(s) objected to; (2) the legal basis supporting the assurance request, including the standards governing the applicable law; and (3) the factual basis supporting the recipient's view that it is exempt, including identification of the conflict between the recipient's conscience or religious beliefs and the application of the provision(s), and the specific contexts, procedures, or health care services at issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitted during an investigation, the notification should include the same information but the factual basis should discuss the specific context of the investigation. A recipient may seek assurance of an exemption applying to categories of procedures or services generally (not necessarily each instance).

rubrics_metrics.name: §92.302(c) — Temporary exemption triggered by notification
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient's notification and request for assurance of an exemption will trigger a temporary exemption covering the time it takes OCR to reach a determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The temporary exemption applies only to the provision(s) as applied to the specific contexts, procedures, or health care services identified in the notification, will exempt conduct occurring during OCR's review and determination, and will serve as a defense to any related investigation or enforcement activity while OCR reviews the request or during any administrative appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: §92.302(c) — Timetable and OCR acknowledgment
rubrics_metrics.description: For pre-enforcement requests, OCR shall provide email confirmation within 30 days acknowledging receipt and stating OCR will work expeditiously to reach a determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the request is received during an investigation, it serves as a defense to the investigation/enforcement activity until final determination, conclusion of the investigation, or during appeal; the temporary exemption remains effective during these periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: §92.302(d) — Effect and scope limitations of an assured exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: An assurance of an exemption exempts the recipient from OCR's administrative investigation and enforcement regarding the application of a particular provision to the specific contexts/procedures/services identified, but does not apply to all contexts or provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recipient must have a legitimate, nondiscriminatory reason for denying or limiting service outside the scope of the granted exemption; decisions outside the exemption cannot be based on unlawful animus or bias or constitute a pretext for discrimination (example: a religious exemption to sterilizations does not permit broadly declining cancer treatments).

rubrics_metrics.name: §92.302(e) — Administrative appeal process
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients subject to an adverse determination of their request for assurance of an exemption may appeal OCR's determination to an administrative hearing examiner from the Department with procedural protections under 45 CFR part 81.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The temporary exemption granted under §92.302(c) remains in effect until completion of the administrative appeal process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case-by-case determination approach
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR will evaluate exemption requests on a case-by-case basis to determine whether a recipient is exempt from the application of certain provisions, or whether modified application is required as to specific contexts, procedures, or services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case-by-case consideration allows OCR to (1) determine whether the government has a compelling interest in denying an exemption, (2) consider any harm an exemption could have on third parties (patients, providers, public), and (3) evaluate whether imposing burdens is the least restrictive means of furthering a compelling government interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal standard application (e.g., RFRA)
rubrics_metrics.description: When administering its exemption process, OCR will apply the legal standards set forth in the Federal religious freedom or conscience law at issue (for example, RFRA's test).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under RFRA, the Government may not substantially burden religious exercise unless it demonstrates (1) the burden furthers a compelling governmental interest; and (2) the burden is the least restrictive means; case law interpreting RFRA requires consideration of potential third-party harms as one of several factors. OCR will also apply different tests where other statutes (e.g., Church Amendments) provide different standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good-faith reliance and relief posture
rubrics_metrics.description: When a recipient acts based upon its good faith reliance that it is exempt from providing a particular medical service due to relevant religious freedom and conscience protections, OCR will not seek backward-looking relief against that recipient even if the recipient had not affirmatively sought assurance under §92.302(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If OCR later determines that the recipient does not satisfy the legal requirements for an exception following an investigation, OCR may seek forward-looking relief as appropriate under the facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification can seek assurance for categories and be used prospectively
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may seek assurance of an exemption applying to specific contexts, procedures, or health care services generally (e.g., a category of procedures) rather than only on an instance-by-instance basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When OCR makes a case-by-case determination, it refers to evaluation of the assurance request as a whole—which may cover categories of procedures—so a recipient need not seek assurance each time the procedure is sought if an exemption already applies for that category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and evidentiary expectations (illustrative example)
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR provided an example of what a notification might include: the provision at issue, the legal basis for exemption, and factual evidence (e.g., that the institution historically never performs sterilization procedures) to support the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such concrete factual and legal information helps OCR assess whether the requested exemption meets the applicable statutory and precedent-based standards (example drawn from investigation of a Catholic hospital refusing a hysterectomy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public reporting of exemption determinations (commenter request)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some commenters urged OCR to publish determinations for any exemptions claimed or granted under §92.302 (e.g., post on website).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters requested transparency in publication of de-identified data on conscience claims and review timelines; earlier in the rule OCR noted it posts resolution agreements and provides information to Congress annually.
